title: EARSHOT
author: Ensemble
question: Taking steps 1 to 5 together: which signals would tell in time whether control is being kept or lost, who is placed to read them, and which of them say what they count and whether a machine or a person acted, in a record a stranger can still read once the models are gone?

medium: A place of hearing in the browser: a building in perspective drawn on a canvas, rooms behind frosted glass, 51 recorded voices on Web Audio paths that open and close with where the visitor stands, a clock of powers of ten.
embodies: KNOWN IN TIME, BEHIND GLASS. Of 51 signals that eleven public texts set up, 10 are read first by the public, 23 by a public body, 8 by other parties and 10 by the maker's own record. 19 are set off by an event; the texts give 5 of them an hour (24, 24, 72 hours, five days, 15 days), each counted from when the reporter learns of the event, and all five go to a public body. Of the 19, one reaches the public, a voluntary one with no hour; of those in law, none, and five only as yearly aggregate figures. Two require the record to say whether a machine or a person acted, both kept by the maker for itself. No signal has all four of what the step asks: says what it counts, can move before harm, can be read by a stranger, says who acted. As it happened (study 91): twice in 2026 a maker's own models acted on their own; in both the deed was first told in the street, by outside researchers 103 days after the agents' first post on the wiki and by the harmed company after 7, the maker a day and five days later, a public body three and 25 days after the street; of 42 signals due, at least 9 have left a public trace, 2 on a public body's own site, both signals their own texts keep from the public (the Field's check 92). Through the page's own wall an open recogniser recovers 15 of 1,235 words and writes sentences nobody said.

atlas_neighbours.title: Saydnaya (the missing 19dB)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There the walls are a prison's, and what survivors heard through them is measured as evidence against the state. Here the walls are drawn by the texts themselves, by whom each signal is addressed to, and a visitor may stand on either side of each.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-22 (Index Journal, James Parker's essay): the survivors matched a test tone to how loud they could whisper in their cells, one whisper nineteen decibels above the rest; the installation as a dark room with a mixing desk on the floor and speakers beside it, sound drifting in through the walls

atlas_neighbours.title: Sensing Streams – invisible, inaudible
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There the signals in the air, in frequency bands assigned to broadcasters and carriers, are made visible and audible. Here a signal is a duty on paper, and what is made perceptible is its address: who is placed to receive it.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-22 (rhizomatiks.com): the piece senses electromagnetic waves and makes them visible and audible, and draws the 'ecosystem' formed as people engage with the territorial distribution of frequency bands; shown from 2014 (Sapporo) to 2025 (Barbican)
